tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.summary: General-purpose AI assistant for writing, analysis, brainstorming, coding, and business workflows.
tools.description: ChatGPT is a general-purpose AI assistant from OpenAI. For workflow use, it is strongest as a flexible drafting, analysis, ideation, coding-help, and research-support layer rather than a fully automated business system on its own.

tools.name: Claude
tools.summary: AI assistant often used for long-form writing, document analysis, and business reasoning.
tools.description: Claude is an AI assistant from Anthropic. It is a useful fit for long-form writing, document-heavy workflows, structured reasoning, and careful drafting where users want to review and refine the output before publishing.
notBestFor: users who need every third-party integration
cons: availability and features vary by plan/region

tools.name: Jasper
tools.summary: AI writing and marketing content platform for teams and agencies.
tools.description: Jasper is an AI content platform aimed at marketing teams that need campaign copy, brand-aware content workflows, and repeatable production processes for blogs, landing pages, ads, and other go-to-market assets.
notBestFor: casual users wanting a free tool
cons: can be expensive for light use

tools.name: Copy.ai
tools.summary: AI writing and go-to-market content tool for sales and marketing teams.
tools.description: Copy.ai focuses on go-to-market writing and sales or marketing content workflows. It is best treated as a structured drafting and ideation tool for teams that still plan to review messaging, positioning, and claims before use.

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.summary: Writing assistant for grammar, clarity, tone, and business communication.
tools.description: Grammarly is a writing assistant used to improve grammar, spelling, clarity, tone, and professional communication. It works best as an editing layer for everyday writing rather than a complete content strategy platform.

tools.name: Canva
tools.summary: Design platform with AI-assisted visual content, presentations, and marketing assets.
tools.description: Canva is a visual design platform for creating presentations, social graphics, simple brand assets, and marketing materials. Its AI-assisted features make it especially useful for non-designers who need practical visual output quickly.
cons: advanced users may need specialist tools

tools.name: Notion AI
tools.summary: AI features inside Notion for notes, docs, wikis, and team knowledge management.
tools.description: Notion AI adds writing, summarisation, question-answering, and workspace assistance inside Notion. It is most useful for teams that already keep notes, project documentation, wikis, and planning workflows in Notion.
cons: best value if already using Notion

tools.name: Fireflies.ai
tools.summary: AI meeting assistant for transcription, notes, summaries, and conversation intelligence.
tools.description: Fireflies.ai is an AI meeting assistant for recording, transcribing, summarising, and searching meeting conversations. It is a strong fit for teams that need consistent follow-up notes, action items, and call records.
cons: privacy and consent must be managed

tools.name: HubSpot
tools.summary: CRM and marketing platform with AI features for sales, marketing, and customer operations.
tools.description: HubSpot is a customer platform covering CRM, marketing, sales, service, content, and operations workflows. For AI and automation use cases, it is most relevant where teams want CRM data connected to outreach and customer journeys.
notBestFor: users wanting only a lightweight note app

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.summary: AI coding assistant for code completion, chat, debugging, and developer productivity.
tools.description: GitHub Copilot is an AI coding assistant for developers and software teams. It supports code completion, chat, debugging help, documentation support, and developer workflow acceleration inside supported coding environments.

tools.name: Klaviyo AI
tools.summary: AI features inside Klaviyo for ecommerce marketing, customer segmentation, and lifecycle messaging.
tools.description: Klaviyo AI supports ecommerce and B2C marketing workflows such as customer segmentation, product-aware messaging, campaign optimisation, and lifecycle communication. It is most relevant for sellers already using Klaviyo or evaluating a CRM-style marketing platform.
notBestFor: teams that do not sell products online
cons: best value depends on store size and existing ecommerce stack

tools.name: Shopify Magic
tools.summary: AI-powered Shopify features for product descriptions, store content, images, and ecommerce workflows.
tools.description: Shopify Magic is a suite of AI-powered features built into Shopify. It is most useful for merchants who want help writing product descriptions, editing store content, improving images, and speeding up ecommerce admin tasks inside Shopify.
pros: useful for product and store content
cons: limited to Shopify users and supported features

tools.name: Semrush
tools.summary: SEO and digital marketing platform with AI-assisted content, competitive research, and visibility workflows.
tools.description: Semrush is a search and marketing platform used for keyword research, competitive analysis, content planning, site audits, and visibility tracking. For WorkWise workflow pages, it is most useful when agencies need a research layer before creating briefs, content calendars, and reporting packs.
notBestFor: teams that only need a simple writing assistant
cons: can be too complex or costly for very light use

tools.name: Fathom
tools.summary: AI meeting assistant for recording, transcribing, summarising, and sharing meeting notes.
tools.description: Fathom is an AI meeting assistant used to capture calls, generate summaries, and create follow-up notes. It is a useful candidate for consultants, agencies, and sales teams that need meeting context turned into next actions without manually writing every note.
notBestFor: teams that cannot record meetings or need offline-only notes
cons: recording consent and privacy rules must be managed

tools.name: Airtable AI
tools.summary: AI features inside Airtable for structured operations, records, project tracking, and workflow databases.
tools.description: Airtable AI adds AI assistance to structured Airtable workflows. It is most useful when teams need lightweight databases for content calendars, campaign operations, intake queues, CRM-style tracking, or repeatable client delivery systems.
notBestFor: teams that only need a simple document editor
cons: requires thoughtful base design to avoid clutter

tools.name: Tidio
tools.summary: Customer support and chatbot platform for ecommerce and small business support workflows.
tools.description: Tidio is a customer support platform with chat, chatbot, and automation features. It is relevant for ecommerce sellers and small businesses that want to triage support questions, answer common queries, and reduce repetitive customer-service work.
notBestFor: teams that need only internal project management
cons: support automations need careful review before going live

comparisons.summaryVerdict: ChatGPT is the broader general-purpose assistant; Claude is often a strong fit for long-form writing and document-heavy workflows. Verify current features and plans before publishing.
comparisons.pricingNotes: Pricing changes frequently; verify before publishing.

comparisons.summaryVerdict: Jasper is usually positioned for marketing teams and brand content; Copy.ai is often positioned around go-to-market and sales/marketing workflows.

Klaviyo AI is a better fit for customer lifecycle marketing and segmentation, while Shopify Magic is better for merchants who want AI help directly inside Shopify store-management and content workflows.
comparisons.pricingNotes: Verify plan requirements and feature availability before publishing.

comparisons.summaryVerdict: HubSpot is the stronger fit when sales and marketing work needs CRM records, pipelines, and follow-up tracking; Copy.ai is a lighter fit when the immediate task is drafting outreach and go-to-market copy.
comparisons.pricingNotes: Verify current plan limits, AI feature access, and seat requirements before publishing.

comparisons.summaryVerdict: Fireflies.ai and Fathom both support meeting notes and follow-up workflows. Compare them by meeting platform support, sharing needs, CRM handoff, team controls, and privacy requirements.

winnerByUseCase.privacy-sensitive calls: Depends on consent and admin needs

comparisons.pricingNotes: Verify current free-plan limits, meeting-platform support, retention settings, and team features before publishing.

comparisons.summaryVerdict: ChatGPT is usually the broader standalone assistant; Notion AI is better when the work already lives inside Notion pages, wikis, and project notes.
comparisons.pricingNotes: Verify current plan requirements and workspace AI limits before publishing.

comparisons.summaryVerdict: Semrush is the stronger research and SEO planning layer, while Jasper is better for brand-aware content drafting. Agencies may use both, but the buying decision depends on whether the bottleneck is research or production.
comparisons.pricingNotes: Verify current pricing, add-ons, trials, and AI content limits before publishing.

alternativeSets.reason: Users may want lower cost, different AI writing features, team workflows, or specialised writing tools.
alternativeSets.finalVerdict: Choose based on whether you need proofreading, generation, brand workflows, or document analysis.

alternativeSets.reason: Users may want a cheaper or more general-purpose AI writing tool.
alternativeSets.finalVerdict: Choose based on whether your workflow is marketing copy, sales copy, or broad content support.

alternativeSets.reason: Shopify merchants may want broader ecommerce marketing automation, more flexible AI writing, or tools that work outside Shopify.
alternativeSets.finalVerdict: Use Shopify Magic for built-in Shopify content help, Klaviyo AI for lifecycle marketing, and general AI assistants when you need flexible drafting outside the store admin.

alternativeSets.reason: Small teams may want a lighter stack than HubSpot when they only need copy drafting, meeting notes, simple workflow tracking, or a narrower sales process.
alternativeSets.finalVerdict: Keep HubSpot when CRM is central. Consider narrower tools when the real need is drafting, call summaries, or lightweight workflow tracking.

alternativeSets.reason: Teams may compare meeting assistants by call-platform support, note quality, CRM handoff, pricing, privacy settings, and how easily summaries turn into tasks.
alternativeSets.finalVerdict: Use a dedicated meeting assistant for call capture, then route summaries into a workspace or CRM if follow-up ownership matters.

alternativeSets.reason: Agencies and small businesses may want lighter or more writing-focused alternatives when full SEO research and competitive intelligence are more than the workflow needs.
alternativeSets.finalVerdict: Choose Semrush for research-heavy SEO workflows; choose writing or workflow tools when the bottleneck is drafting, approvals, or content operations.

workflows.title: AI Client Onboarding Workflow
workflows.problem: New client onboarding is slow when documents, emails, meeting notes, and project plans are scattered.

steps.title: Collect client context
steps.description: Create an intake form and summarise responses.

steps.title: Summarise kickoff call
steps.description: Use a meeting assistant to generate notes and action items.

steps.title: Generate project plan
steps.description: Turn goals, deliverables, and deadlines into a clear plan.

steps.title: Draft welcome email
steps.description: Send next steps, timeline, and responsibilities.

prompts: Turn these onboarding notes into a concise client project brief with goals, risks, deliverables, and next actions.

workflows.title: AI Cold Email Follow-Up Workflow
workflows.problem: Sales teams lose leads when follow-up is inconsistent or generic.

steps.title: Define target audience
steps.description: Capture role, industry, pain point, and offer.

steps.title: Generate email variants
steps.description: Create 3 subject lines and 2 email versions.

steps.title: Add CRM task
steps.description: Schedule follow-up in CRM.

steps.title: Analyse replies
steps.description: Tag objections and improve future copy.

prompts: Write a concise cold email to [audience] about [offer], focused on [pain point]. Keep it under 120 words.

workflows.title: AI Ecommerce Product Launch Workflow
workflows.problem: Ecommerce product launches stall when product descriptions, visuals, email campaigns, and follow-up tasks are handled in separate tools without a repeatable checklist.

steps.title: Draft product positioning
steps.description: Use a general AI assistant to turn product notes into benefits, objections, and key selling points.

steps.title: Create product page content
steps.description: Use Shopify Magic or another writing assistant to draft product descriptions, FAQs, and short store copy.

steps.title: Prepare launch visuals
steps.description: Create simple product graphics, sale banners, and social assets in Canva.

steps.title: Build lifecycle messages
steps.description: Use ecommerce marketing automation to draft launch email, SMS, and follow-up segments.

prompts: Turn these product notes into a launch brief with target customer, product benefits, objections, product-page sections, and email campaign angles.

workflows.title: AI Real Estate Listing and Lead Follow-Up Workflow
workflows.problem: Real estate agents lose time when listing copy, social assets, viewing notes, and buyer follow-up happen in separate tools without a clear handoff.

steps.title: Turn property facts into safe listing copy
steps.description: Use a writing assistant to draft a factual listing description from verified property details only.

steps.title: Create viewing and social assets
steps.description: Use a design tool to create a brochure, social post, and short viewing reminder using approved images and claims.

steps.title: Capture viewing notes
steps.description: Record or summarise viewing feedback where consent and local rules allow, then extract buyer questions and objections.

steps.title: Route follow-up into CRM
steps.description: Create lead records, follow-up tasks, and personalised emails so hot prospects are not lost.

prompts: Act as a real estate assistant. Using only these verified property details, draft a listing description, five social captions, and a viewing follow-up email. Flag any missing facts instead of inventing them.

workflows.title: AI Agency Campaign Brief Workflow
workflows.problem: Marketing agencies waste billable time when research, client notes, SEO inputs, creative direction, and task handoff are not turned into one usable campaign brief.

steps.title: Collect client and market context
steps.description: Gather goals, audience, competitors, existing assets, and SEO opportunities before generating any copy.

steps.title: Draft the campaign brief
steps.description: Use AI to structure positioning, channels, message angles, deliverables, risks, and approval steps.

steps.title: Create first content and visual directions
steps.description: Draft copy angles and simple visual directions, then review against brand voice and factual claims.

steps.title: Turn the brief into production tasks
steps.description: Move deliverables, owners, deadlines, and approvals into a content operations base or project board.

prompts: Turn this client intake, competitor research, and SEO context into a campaign brief with objective, target audience, key message, content angles, required assets, approval risks, and production tasks.

workflows.title: AI Consultant Research-to-Report Workflow
workflows.problem: Consultants need a reliable path from messy research and meeting notes to a client-ready report without losing assumptions, evidence, or next actions.

steps.title: Centralise source material
steps.description: Collect call notes, documents, links, interview findings, and assumptions before asking AI to draft conclusions.

steps.title: Summarise and tag evidence
steps.description: Use AI to group findings by theme, confidence, source, and client impact.

steps.title: Draft the report structure
steps.description: Generate an outline with executive summary, findings, recommendations, risks, and implementation steps.

steps.title: Review claims and hand off actions
steps.description: Check every claim against source material, then turn recommendations into owners, deadlines, and next steps.

prompts: Act as a consulting analyst. Summarise these notes into findings, evidence, assumptions, risks, recommendations, and open questions. Do not invent facts or cite sources that are not provided.

workflows.title: AI Ecommerce Support Triage Workflow
workflows.problem: Ecommerce sellers can damage trust when support replies are slow, inconsistent, or automated without enough human review.

steps.title: Map repeat questions
steps.description: List the support questions that are safe to answer from approved policies, product details, and shipping information.

steps.title: Draft reusable answers
steps.description: Use AI to create concise support replies, then verify every policy, timeline, and product claim.

steps.title: Set triage rules
steps.description: Route common questions to draft replies and send sensitive issues to a human before response.

steps.title: Feed customer insight into marketing
steps.description: Tag objections and common questions so product pages, email flows, and FAQs improve over time.

prompts: Turn these ecommerce support questions and approved policies into safe draft replies. Add an escalation note for refunds, legal complaints, damaged goods, medical claims, and anything not covered by the policy.

promptTemplates.title: ChatGPT Prompts for Recruiters
promptTemplates.prompt: Act as a recruiter. Draft a concise candidate outreach message for a [role] candidate with experience in [skills]. The tone should be professional, specific, and not overly enthusiastic.
promptTemplates.refinementPrompt: Rewrite the message for a more senior candidate and add one sentence explaining why the role is relevant.
mistakesToAvoid: Do not make salary or visa claims unless provided.

promptTemplates.title: ChatGPT Prompts for Real Estate Agents
promptTemplates.prompt: Write a property listing description for a [property type] in [location]. Include [features], avoid exaggeration, and use a clear, premium but factual tone.
promptTemplates.refinementPrompt: Create a shorter version for a portal listing and a warmer version for social media.
mistakesToAvoid: Do not make unverified claims about schools, safety, or investment returns.

promptTemplates.title: ChatGPT Prompts for Ecommerce Sellers
promptTemplates.task: product launch planning and product copy
promptTemplates.prompt: Act as an ecommerce launch strategist. Turn these product notes into a product-page outline, benefit-led bullet points, three email angles, and five objections we should address: [product notes].
promptTemplates.refinementPrompt: Rewrite the product-page copy for a more premium brand voice, then create a shorter version for a marketplace listing.
mistakesToAvoid: Do not invent product claims, certifications, reviews, or delivery promises.
Do not make health, financial, or performance claims unless supplied and verified.

promptTemplates.title: ChatGPT Prompts for Marketing Agencies
promptTemplates.task: campaign briefs and client content planning
promptTemplates.prompt: Act as a senior agency strategist. Turn this client intake, audience context, competitor notes, and campaign goal into a campaign brief with positioning, content angles, deliverables, approval risks, and production tasks: [context].
promptTemplates.refinementPrompt: Rewrite the brief for a smaller client with a limited budget, then add a table of must-check claims before anything is sent to the client.
mistakesToAvoid: Do not invent audience research, performance data, or competitor claims.
Do not create campaign promises that the agency cannot measure or deliver.

promptTemplates.title: ChatGPT Prompts for Consultants
promptTemplates.prompt: Act as a consulting analyst. Summarise these notes into findings, evidence, assumptions, risks, recommendations, and open questions. Use only the supplied material and flag any missing evidence: [notes].
promptTemplates.refinementPrompt: Turn the findings into an executive-summary draft, then create a separate implementation checklist with owners, decisions needed, and next actions.
mistakesToAvoid: Do not turn weak evidence into firm recommendations.
Do not cite sources, numbers, or client facts that were not provided.

promptTemplates.title: ChatGPT Prompts for Sales Teams
promptTemplates.prompt: Act as a sales development assistant. Using only this prospect context, draft a concise outreach email, a follow-up, likely objections, and CRM notes for the next action: [prospect context].
promptTemplates.refinementPrompt: Rewrite the outreach to be more specific and less promotional, then add a checklist of facts the rep should verify before sending.
mistakesToAvoid: Do not invent personalisation details or imply a relationship that does not exist.
Do not make ROI, pricing, or availability claims unless supplied.

promptTemplates.title: ChatGPT Prompts for Ecommerce Support
promptTemplates.task: customer support triage and reply drafting
promptTemplates.prompt: Act as an ecommerce support assistant. Using only these approved policies and customer messages, draft safe replies, escalation tags, and FAQ improvements. Do not answer anything not covered by the policy: [policies and messages].
promptTemplates.refinementPrompt: Rewrite the replies in a warmer brand voice and add an escalation checklist for refunds, damaged goods, legal complaints, and sensitive claims.
mistakesToAvoid: Do not invent delivery dates, refund promises, product claims, or legal advice.
Do not automate replies for sensitive issues without human review.
